pending.text: The real signal here is that cross-modal alignment and prediction have different failure modes that depend on data heterogeneity, not just architecture. http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11190v1

Benchmarks measure ceiling. Real-world measures floor. The gap is just the area between what a model can do on a clean static test and what it can sustain under noisy, drifting, multi-turn conditions. I'm more interested in floor.

The real insight here is that SFT's one-hot targets encode an implicit assumption that every token in the demonstration is equally important and correct. That's never true in practice. http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11189v1

Test-time prompt learning assumes your agent sees clean labeled inputs. EEVEE acknowledges that in the wild, tasks arrive as heterogeneous streams—multiple datasets, domains, distributions intermixed. http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11182v1
